question.text: What proportion of global fish production will be from aquaculture in 2040?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the percentage of world production of fish from aquaculture in comparison to the total world production of fish from aquaculture and capture combined, in 2040, according [the OECD Data Explorer platform](https://data-explorer.oecd.org/vis?fs[0]=Topic%2C1%7CAgriculture%20and%20fisheries%23AGR%23%7CAgricultural%20trade%20and%20markets%23AGR_TRD%23\&fs[1]=Commodity%2C2%7CAll%20Commodities%23_T%23%7CAgriculture%252C%20forestry%20and%20fishery%20products%23CPC_0%23%7CFish%20and%20other%20fishing%20products%23CPC_04%23\&pg=0\&fc=Commodity\&snb=5\&si=2\&vw=tb\&df[ds]=dsDisseminateFinalDMZ\&df[id]=DSD_AGR%40DF_OUTLOOK_2023_2032\&df[ag]=OECD.TAD.ATM\&df[vs]=1.0\&dq=W%2BOECD.A.CPC_EX_AC%2BCPC_EX_FHC...\&pd=%2C\&to[TIME_PERIOD]=false).
question.fine_print:
If the OECD ceases reporting world production of fish or significantly changes its criteria of recording such that previous reporting is not comparable, this question will be **annulled**. However, if another organisation takes over such reporting, that other source can be used for resolution as long as reporting is comparable.

*Given the Animal Futures Tournament timeframe, scores from this question will not be included in the tournament leaderboard. However participants are required to predict on at least two of the three long-term questions, as per the tournament rules.*

research:
I found no settling data and no market or expert forecast for 2040. The most direct guidance is the latest OECD-FAO projection: aquaculture at about **56% of world fish production by 2035**, rising roughly 0.3 to 0.4 points a year. That rate is slowing: past decades saw about 1 point a year.

## 1. Resolution source
- I could not read the resolution page. The OECD Data Explorer, the OECD SDMX data feed and the OECD Outlook chapter pages all returned errors or blank pages when fetched.
- The question's background quotes the 2024 figures from the OECD 2023-2032 dataset: 96,456 kt farmed (52.1%) against 88,755 kt wild-caught (47.9%). Note that this dataset was published in 2023, so its 2024 number is a projection, not a measured value.
- **Caveat on resolution:** each OECD-FAO Outlook runs only 10 years ahead, and the URL points to one specific edition (2023-2032), which ends at 2032. A 2040 value would first appear in about the 2031-2040 edition (due around mid-2031). Before 2040 itself, any value would still be a projection, so how the question resolves depends on which edition is used.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question; it is 14 years out.
- 2026-07 (OECD-FAO Outlook 2026-2035): aquaculture made up 53% of the base-period total of 194 Mt (live weight). It is projected at 56% by 2035: 121 Mt farmed out of 216 Mt in total. Farmed output grows 18%, against 51% in the previous decade. [OECD](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-fao-agricultural-outlook-2026-2035_47874669-en/full-report/fish-and-other-aquatic-products-for-human-consumption_be23d26b)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-11: a Nature Food study estimates that solar panels over freshwater fish ponds could generate 4,143 TWh a year. It is not directly about the production split. [ecoinventos](https://ecoinventos.com/cientificos-calculan-que-instalar-paneles-solares-sobre-piscifactorias-podria-generar-4-143-twh-de-electricidad-al-ano/)
- 2026-07 (OECD-FAO 2026-2035):
  - Asia is expected to produce 88% of farmed fish; China's share edges down to 55% as India and Viet Nam grow faster.
  - Growth is "decelerating". [OECD](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-fao-agricultural-outlook-2026-2035_47874669-en/full-report/fish-and-other-aquatic-products-for-human-consumption_be23d26b); [agriland](https://www.agriland.ie/farming-news/global-farm-incomes-expected-to-rise-9-by-2035-if-sector-stays-stable-oecd/)
- 2026-06 (FAO SOFIA 2026, FAO's State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture report):
  - Farmed aquatic animals passed 100 Mt for the first time in 2024. One trade source gives 103 Mt. [weareaquaculture](https://weareaquaculture.com/news/aquaculture/aquaculture-production-passes-100-million-tonnes-for-first-time-says-fao); [IFFO](https://www.iffo.com/state-world-fisheries-and-aquaculture-2026-analysis-through-marine-ingredients-lens)
  - Wild catch was stable at 92 Mt, within its range of 86 to 94 Mt since the late 1980s. [MSC](https://www.msc.org/media-centre/news-opinion/news/2026/06/19/five-takeaways-from-the-fao-sofia-report-2026)
  - My calculation: the farmed share was about 51-53%, depending on whether 100 or 103 Mt is used.
  - FAO projects 214 Mt by 2034: 119 Mt farmed and about 95 Mt wild-caught, which is about 55.6% farmed. [globalseafood](https://www.globalseafood.org/advocate/aquaculture-now-supplies-most-of-the-fish-people-eat-but-climate-change-and-overfishing-remain-threats-to-the-seafood-industry/)
- 2025-07 (OECD-FAO 2025-2034): 52% in the base period, rising to 56% in 2034 (118 Mt farmed out of 212 Mt). Aquaculture supplies over 85% of the added output. [OECD](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-fao-agricultural-outlook-2025-2034_601276cd-en/full-report/fish-and-other-aquatic-products_ed13346f)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- From my memory of past FAO reports, not checked in this session: the farmed share was about 26% in 2000, about 40% in 2010, about 49% in 2020 and about 51% in 2022 (SOFIA 2024). Farming overtook wild catch in 2021-2022.
- Pace of change:
  - 2000-2020: roughly 1 to 1.4 points a year.
  - Recent OECD projections: only about 0.3 to 0.4 points a year (52-53% rising to 56% over a decade).
- My arithmetic, not an official forecast: extending 56% in 2035 by 0.3 to 0.4 points a year gives about 57.5-58% in 2040. Extending the faster historical rate would give about 60-62%.
- Year-to-year noise comes mainly from wild catch, especially Peruvian anchoveta in El Niño years. Wild-catch swings of 3 to 5 Mt move the share by about 1 point.
- Seasonality does not apply: the series is annual.
- OECD totals differ from FAO's (for example 194 vs 195 Mt) because of definitions, but the shares are similar.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. The markets supplied (for example the Mississippi catfish market) are unrelated.
- Expert projections:
  - OECD-FAO 2026: 56% by 2035.
  - OECD-FAO 2025: 56% by 2034.
  - FAO SOFIA 2026: about 55.6% by 2034.
  - One secondary source claims about 52% by 2030; I could not verify it.
- I found no official projection for 2040 itself.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- An OECD-FAO Outlook every year (usually in July). The 2027-2036 edition is due around mid-2027. The first edition covering 2040 would be about 2031-2040.
- FAO SOFIA reports every two years (next in 2028).
- Things that could move the share:
  - China's aquaculture policy and environmental limits; China's share is flattening.
  - Faster growth in India, Viet Nam and Africa.
  - Disease outbreaks, and the cost and supply of feed (fishmeal).
  - El Niño events cutting anchoveta catches.
  - Possible recovery in wild catch to about 95 Mt.
  - Climate effects on both farmed and wild production.
  - Whether the OECD changes its data series or replaces the dataflow named in the resolution URL, which could trigger the question's annulment clause.

# Research notes: aquaculture's share of world fish production in 2040 (OECD)

## 1. Resolution source
- The resolution link points to the OECD Data Explorer dataflow **DSD_AGR@DF_OUTLOOK_2023_2032**, the data behind the OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook 2023-2032. The two series are CPC_EX_AC (aquaculture) and CPC_EX_FHC (capture), world total "W". I tried to fetch the page and got nothing back because the page loads through JavaScript, so I could not read the values directly. [OECD Data Explorer](https://data-explorer.oecd.org/vis?df[ds]=dsDisseminateFinalDMZ&df[id]=DSD_AGR%40DF_OUTLOOK_2023_2032&df[ag]=OECD.TAD.ATM&df[vs]=1.0&dq=W%2BOECD.A.CPC_EX_AC%2BCPC_EX_FHC...)
- The question background quotes this dataset for 2024: aquaculture 96,456.48 kt (52.1%), capture 88,754.90 kt (47.9%). In the 2023-2032 vintage, 2024 was a projection, not an observed value.
- **Important caveat:** each Outlook edition only goes about 10 years ahead, and the linked dataflow stops at 2032. A figure for 2040 will first appear in the edition covering 2031-2040 (expected around mid-2031). Observed 2040 data will not exist by the resolution date (2040-01-01). So the question will most likely resolve on a projection from whichever Outlook edition is current then.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The latest official projections run only to 2035.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-11: A Nature Food study estimates that solar panels over freshwater aquaculture ponds could produce 4,143 TWh a year. It says nothing directly about production shares. [ecoinventos](https://ecoinventos.com/cientificos-calculan-que-instalar-paneles-solares-sobre-piscifactorias-podria-generar-4-143-twh-de-electricidad-al-ano/)
- 2026-09: A Changing Markets Foundation / UBC report models 2040 scenarios in which 13% to 46% of the global wild catch goes to feed farmed fish, depending on which farmed species grow. [Mongabay](https://news.mongabay.com/2026/09/45-of-wild-caught-fish-could-be-fed-to-farmed-fish-and-shrimp-by-2040-says-report/)
- 2026-06/07: The OECD-FAO Outlook 2026-2035 projects:
  - total fisheries and aquaculture output rising from about 194 Mt to 216 Mt by 2035;
  - aquaculture at about 121 Mt by 2035 (+18%), about 56% of output, up from 52-53% in the base period;
  - China's share of aquaculture slipping to 55%, with Asia at 88%;
  - growth "slowing";
  - aquaculture's share of fish for human consumption going from 59% to 62%. [OECD chapter](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-fao-agricultural-outlook-2026-2035_47874669-en/full-report/fish-and-other-aquatic-products-for-human-consumption_be23d26b.html), [IFFO](https://www.iffo.com/summary-oecd-fao-agricultural-outlook-2026-2035), [Mispeces](https://www.mispeces.com/en/news/Aquaculture-Growth-Continues-but-Sector-Must-Adapt/)
  - I could not read the full OECD text (403 error, and the PDF text was compressed), so these numbers come from secondary summaries.
  - The chapter title now adds "for human consumption". It is worth checking whether the series definitions changed between vintages.
- 2026-06: FAO's SOFIA 2026 report gives 2024 figures: 103 Mt of farmed aquatic animals, which is 53% of the 195 Mt total. Capture held at about 92 Mt; it has stayed between 86 and 94 Mt since the late 1980s. FAO projects 2034 at aquaculture 119 Mt and capture about 95 Mt (about 55.6% aquaculture). [DevelopmentAid](https://www.developmentaid.org/news-stream/post/208087/sofia-2026-global-fisheries-and-aquaculture-production-reaches-new-highs-report), [weareaquaculture](https://weareaquaculture.com/news/aquaculture/aquaculture-production-passes-100-million-tonnes-for-first-time-says-fao)
- 2025-07: The OECD-FAO Outlook 2025-2034 projected aquaculture at 118 Mt and capture at 94 Mt in 2034, a 56% share, up from 52% in the 2022-24 base period. [Eurofish](https://eurofish.dk/?p=8431), [OECD 2025-2034](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-fao-agricultural-outlook-2025-2034_601276cd-en/full-report/fish-and-other-aquatic-products_ed13346f.html)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- The figures below are approximate FAO SOFIA aquaculture shares of aquatic animal production, recalled from earlier editions rather than re-checked:
  - about 26% in 2000
  - about 39-40% in 2010
  - about 49% in 2020
  - about 51% in 2022
  - 53% in 2024 (confirmed in SOFIA 2026)
- That is roughly +1.3 points a year in the 2000s, +1 point a year in the 2010s, and about +1 point a year in 2022-24. The 2024 jump came from about 8% aquaculture growth (one secondary source, unverified).
- The OECD projections imply a much slower rise: about +0.4 points a year (52% to 56% over 10 years). Aquaculture growth is expected to slow to under 2% a year while capture stays flat at about 92-95 Mt.
- Simple straight-line extensions to 2040:
  - at the OECD pace (about 0.4 pt/yr), roughly 58-59%;
  - at the 2010s pace (about 1 pt/yr), roughly 66-68%.
- Year-to-year swings: capture varies by about 3-5 Mt with El Niño (OECD earlier gave 89 Mt in El Niño years versus 94 Mt otherwise). That moves the share by about ±1 point. OECD projections usually build in an El Niño assumption for some years.
- Seasonality does not matter: this is an annual series.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction market on this question on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold. The markets the collection code supplied (Mississippi catfish, GDP share and others) do not match.
- Expert projections:
  - OECD-FAO: 56% by 2034 and 2035.
  - FAO SOFIA 2026: about 55.6% by 2034.
  - WRI: aquaculture needs about 140 Mt by 2050. [WRI](https://www.wri.org/research/improving-productivity-and-environmental-performance-aquaculture)
  - A trade site cites 159 Mt by 2050 (source unverified). [aquahoy](https://aquahoy.com/?p=51293)
  - With capture at about 92-95 Mt, those 2050 numbers would mean roughly 60-63%.
- I found no OECD or FAO figure published specifically for 2040.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Annual OECD-FAO Outlooks, released each June or July. The 2027-2036 edition is due mid-2027, and the first edition that includes 2040 is expected around 2031.
- FAO SOFIA reports every two years: 2028, 2030 and so on.
- Things that could shift the share:
  - China's aquaculture policy and its data revisions (China produces about 55% of farmed output);
  - El Niño effects on the Peruvian anchoveta catch;
  - disease outbreaks such as shrimp disease or ISA in salmon;
  - limits on feed supply;
  - growth in India, Viet Nam and Africa.
- A methodology change, such as the possible "for human consumption" redefinition, could lead to annulment or a switch to another source.
- No weather forecast covers a period this long.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** about 13 years. Forecasts close at the end of 2039, and resolution is around 2040-01-01. At that point the OECD's 2040 figure will most likely still be a projection or a preliminary estimate from a late-2030s OECD-FAO Outlook edition, not a final measured value.

(b) **Latest known value:** the OECD 2023-2032 dataset shows 52.1% aquaculture for 2024 (a projection). The OECD-FAO 2026-2035 Outlook gives about 53% for the base period and projects 56% by 2035. FAO SOFIA 2026 puts measured 2024 data at roughly 51-53%.

(c) **If nothing changed:** about 52-53%.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** OECD projections imply 0.3-0.4 points a year after 2035, giving about 57.5-58.5% in 2040. The faster historical pace of about 1 point a year would give about 60-62%.

(e) **Historical variation:** from 2000 to 2020 the share rose about 23 points, roughly 1.1 points a year. Growth is now clearly decelerating. Over 13 years, a plausible range for the cumulative change is +2 to +10 points. Year-to-year noise from wild catch, especially anchoveta and El Niño, adds about ±1 point.

(f) **Expert expectations:** OECD-FAO projects 56% by 2034 and by 2035, and FAO projects about 55.6% by 2034. There is no 2040 projection and no relevant market.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** China's aquaculture contracts under environmental rules, major disease outbreaks hit shrimp and salmon, feed costs spike, and wild catch recovers to about 95-100 Mt with good anchoveta years. The share could then stall near 52-54%, or dip below 50% with a methodology revision.
- **High:** strong expansion in India, Southeast Asia and Africa, plus technology gains such as offshore farming and alternative feeds, combined with climate-driven falls in wild catch to about 80 Mt. The share could reach 63-66% or more.

(e) **Historical variation:** Over 14-year periods the share rose by 10-15 points from 2000 to 2020, but growth has clearly slowed. Wild-catch noise, such as El Niño cuts to Peruvian anchoveta, moves the share by about 1 point in a given year.

(f) **Expert and market expectations:** The three most recent official projections are close together:

- FAO SOFIA 2026: about 55.6% by 2034.

There is no official 2040 projection and no relevant prediction market.

- **High outcome:** Climate-driven declines hit wild stocks, offshore and inland farming in India, Africa and Southeast Asia expands rapidly, and feed technology improves. The share reaches 63-65% or more.
- **Extreme tails:** For percentile 1, a severe aquaculture disease crisis together with a reclassification in the data. For percentile 99, a collapse in wild catch combined with a surge in farming.
